# Front-end assets (CSS, Sass/SCSS, Less, HTML templates, images, fonts)

This reference is about *paths inside stylesheets, templates and asset folders*, which break
silently: no test fails, no build fails (often there is no build), the page just loses a font or
an image, and someone notices in production. Load it whenever the inventory shows `.css`, `.scss`,
`.less`, `.html` or template files, or an `img/`, `images/`, `fonts/`, `static/`, `public/` or
`assets/` directory that the plan touches. It is not a guide to organising CSS (BEM, ITCSS…): that
is design advice, outside "move without changing behaviour".

## How references resolve
- **CSS `url()`** — relative to the *stylesheet's own location*, not the HTML page and not the
  project root (`url(../img/x.png)` inside `css/site.css` means `img/x.png`). Moving a stylesheet
  changes the base of every `url()` in it; moving an asset folder breaks every `url()` that points
  at it. Root-relative `url(/static/x.png)` resolves against the web root, which is a *deployment*
  path (see below). Data URIs and `http(s)://` need nothing.
- **CSS `@import`** — same rule as `url()`; the browser fetches it at runtime unless a bundler
  inlines it.
- **Sass `@use` / `@forward` / `@import`** — resolve against the importing file's directory, then
  each `--load-path` / `includePaths` / `loadPaths` entry. A specifier `foo` matches `foo.scss`,
  `_foo.scss` (partial), `foo/_index.scss`, `foo/index.scss`, and `.sass` variants. A bare name
  with no `./` can also be a `node_modules` package (`@use 'bootstrap/scss/bootstrap'` with a
  load path on `node_modules`). `url()` inside Sass is **not rewritten** by Sass itself: after
  compilation it is relative to the *output* CSS file, so moving sources without moving outputs
  changes nothing for the browser, but moving the output folder does.
- **Less `@import`** — relative to the importing file, then `paths` option; `.less` extension
  optional; `@import (reference)` / `(css)` variants. `url()` is rewritten only with
  `relativeUrls: true` / `rewriteUrls` — check the compiler options before assuming either.
- **PostCSS / Tailwind** — `postcss-import` resolves like Sass (node resolution + `path` option);
  Tailwind's `content` (v3) or `@source` (v4) globs decide which templates are scanned: a template
  folder moved outside those globs loses all its classes in the built CSS, with no error.
- **HTML / templates** (`<link href>`, `<script src>`, `<img src>`, `srcset`, `<source src>`,
  `<a href>`, `<use href>` in inline SVG, `<form action>`): relative to the *URL of the page*,
  which for a static site is the HTML file's location, and for a server-rendered app is the
  route, not the template file. Templates (Smarty, Blade, Twig, Jinja, EJS, ERB, PHP) usually
  reference assets through a helper (`asset()`, `url()`, `{{ static_url }}`, `$baseurl`) with a
  root-relative string: those are deployment paths, pinned by the web-server config.
- **JS imports of assets** — `import './x.module.css'`, `import logo from './logo.svg'`,
  `new URL('./img.png', import.meta.url)`, `require('./x.css')`: bundler-resolved, relative to the
  JS file. `check_moves.py` resolves the first two forms; `new URL(…, import.meta.url)` and
  dynamic `${}` paths are grep-only.
- **Fonts** — `@font-face { src: url(…) }` plus `<link rel="preload" as="font" href>` in HTML:
  two places to update for one move.
- **Source maps** — `/*# sourceMappingURL=site.css.map */` and the `sources` array inside `.map`
  files: regenerate rather than edit.

## Files that pin paths — check every one
| File | What |
|---|---|
| `*.css`, `*.scss`, `*.sass`, `*.less` | `url()`, `@import`, `@use`, `@forward`, `@font-face src`, `sourceMappingURL` |
| `*.html`, templates (`.tpl`, `.blade.php`, `.twig`, `.jinja`, `.ejs`, `.erb`, `.hbs`, `.vue` `<template>`) | `href`, `src`, `srcset`, `poster`, `data-*` URLs, inline `style="background:url()"`, `<base href>` |
| `tailwind.config.*`, CSS `@source` / `@config` (Tailwind v4) | `content` globs over template paths |
| `postcss.config.*`, `.postcssrc*` | `postcss-import` `path`, plugin options with paths |
| `sass` / `node-sass` / `sass-loader` options, `vite.config.*` (`css.preprocessorOptions`), `webpack.mix.js`, `gulpfile.js`, `Gruntfile.js`, `package.json` scripts | `loadPaths` / `includePaths`, input/output pairs (`sass src/scss:public/css`), watch globs |
| `.less` compiler calls (`lessc`, `less.php`, `Less_Parser->SetImportDirs`) | import dirs, `relativeUrls` |
| `manifest.json`, `mix-manifest.json`, `asset-manifest.json`, `.vite/manifest.json` | hashed output paths; regenerated by the build, never edited |
| `robots.txt`, `sitemap*.xml`, `_redirects`, `netlify.toml`, `vercel.json`, `.htaccess`, `nginx.conf`, `web.config` | public URLs, rewrites, cache rules per folder (`/static/`, `/assets/`) |
| `<link rel="icon">`, `site.webmanifest`, `browserconfig.xml`, Open Graph `og:image`, `<link rel="canonical">` | absolute or root-relative asset URLs that crawlers and browsers cache |
| Framework config | Django `STATIC_URL`/`STATICFILES_DIRS`/`STATIC_ROOT`, `TEMPLATES[DIRS]`; Flask `static_folder`/`template_folder`; Laravel `resources/`, `public/build`; Symfony `assets/`, `importmap.php`, `webpack.config.js` (Encore); Rails `app/assets`, `config/manifest.js`; Next `public/`; Astro/Eleventy `passthroughCopy` |
| Email templates, PDF templates (wkhtmltopdf, Dompdf) | absolute `file://` or `http://` asset URLs frozen in the template |
| Service worker (`sw.js`, Workbox config) | precache lists of asset URLs |

## Runtime references to grep for
```
url(            @import         @use            @forward        src=            href=
srcset=         poster=         sourceMappingURL                asset(          static(
STATIC_URL      STATICFILES     template_folder static_folder   includePaths    loadPaths
content: [      @source         passthroughCopy  mix(           Vite::          importmap
```
Also grep every *asset folder name* you move (`img/`, `fonts/`) across `*.html`, `*.css`, `*.js`,
templates and server config: assets are referenced by string far more often than code is.

## Idiomatic layouts (keep what the project already does)
- **Static site**: `index.html` at the root or in `public/`; one of `css/ js/ img/ fonts/` or a single
  `assets/{css,js,img,fonts}/`. Moving between these two conventions rewrites every `url()`, `href`
  and `src`: only worth it if the plan already touches most templates.
- **Preprocessor sources vs outputs**: `src/scss/` (or `resources/sass/`, `assets/styles/`) compiled
  to `public/css/` (or `dist/css/`). Outputs are build products: if they are committed, decide
  whether to move them with the sources (and keep the compiler's output option in sync) or to stop
  committing them — both are user decisions, put them in the plan.
- **Component-scoped styles** (CSS Modules, Vue/Svelte SFC, styled-components): the stylesheet lives
  next to its component and moves with it; nothing else references it.
- **Framework-fixed folders** (Django `static/`+`templates/` per app, Laravel `resources/`+`public/`,
  Rails `app/assets/`, Next `public/`): the framework resolves them by convention — leave them in
  place and restructure inside them.

## Tooling and verification
- **Build the CSS before and after** when a compiler exists: `sass`, `lessc`, `postcss`, `tailwindcss`,
  `vite build`, `npm run build` — add the command to `baseline.py` with `--extra` if it is not
  detected. Compare the *output* files byte for byte (or after stripping the source-map comment):
  for a pure move of sources, the compiled CSS must be identical.
- **Resolve every reference on disk**: `check_moves.py` resolves relative `url()`, `@import`, `@use`,
  `@forward` in `.css/.scss/.sass/.less` (with partial and index conventions, `--load-path` not
  included) and relative `src`/`href`/`srcset`/`poster` in `.html` and template files, and lists the
  ones that no longer point at a file. Root-relative (`/static/x.png`) and helper-generated URLs
  are not resolved: check them against the web-root mapping by hand.
- **Serve and look**: for a static site, `python3 -m http.server` in the web root and a crawl with
  `wget --spider -r -nd -l 3 http://localhost:8000/` (or `linkchecker`) lists every 404 — the
  cheapest end-to-end check there is. Record the crawl output before and after in the evidence folder.
- **Browser check** when available: open the main pages, read the console for failed requests
  (`Failed to load resource`), compare screenshots. Say in the validation report which pages were
  looked at and which were not.
- **Stylelint**, `html-validate`, `htmlhint` when configured: counts before/after like any linter.

## Traps
- `url()` is relative to the **stylesheet**, `href`/`src` in HTML to the **page URL**: the same
  string in the two places means two different files.
- Moving a stylesheet one level deeper silently breaks every `url(../…)` in it, and the page
  still renders — with missing images, fallback fonts and broken icons.
- Sass `url()` is not rewritten: moving *sources* is safe for the browser, moving the *output
  directory* is not; Less with `relativeUrls: true` is the opposite.
- Tailwind `content` globs: a template folder moved outside the glob compiles to a CSS file that
  lacks every class used there. The build succeeds. Compare the output size and class list.
- **Compiled template caches** (Smarty `templates_c/` or its configured compile dir, Twig cache, Blade
  `storage/framework/views`) store paths resolved at compile time — the template source and, for
  Smarty, the `include` of every plugin file the template uses. After the library or the templates
  move, a page compiled before the move can fail (`Call to undefined function smarty_modifier_…`)
  until the cache is purged. Make the purge a deployment step in the validation report, and test it
  by hand, not as a gate: deploy the old commit, render, deploy the branch over it, render again —
  once without purging (expected to fail: that is the evidence the purge is needed) and once with
  the purge. Keep both outputs in the evidence folder. As a `--extra` gate it proves nothing at
  record-before (old and new are the same commit there).
- Case-sensitive servers: `Img/Logo.PNG` works on macOS and Windows, 404s on Linux. A move is the
  moment this bites; resolve references case-sensitively, as `check_moves.py` does on Linux.
- Hashed filenames (`site.3f9a.css`) come from a manifest — edit the source path in the build
  config, never the manifest, and rebuild.
- CDN and cache rules keyed by folder (`/static/` cached one year): a moved asset under a new
  folder may lose or gain caching; mention it in the plan if the server config has such rules.
- Email and PDF templates with absolute URLs keep working after a move *only because* they point
  at the deployed site: they are not broken by the migration, they are broken by the deployment
  that follows if the public paths changed — list them under "References to update".
